text.p: Hughes Electronics Corp and Northrop Grumman Corp both declined comment on Monday about the ongoing bidding war for the General Motors Co unit's missile and radar businesses.
"I have no comment as a matter of policy," said Jim Hart of Northrop. A spokewoman for Hughes also declined comment.
Earlier Raytheon Co declined to comment on reports is it the leading bidder for the Hughes assets.
"We continue to have no comment on merger and acquisition speculation," spokesman Robert McWade said.
A source familiar with the auction told Reuters on Monday that an announcement by Wednesday is unlikely and that the process may drag out to later in the week.

Sources following the auction told Reuters on Friday that Raytheon's and rival Northrop's bids for the General Motors unit ranged from $9.8 billion to $10.4 billion. The Wall Street Journal reported Monday that Raytheon was leading in the bidding with a proposal of about $9.5 billion.
